author: jasdeepbhalla
body:
### Issue # (if applicable)

Closes #36348.

### Reason for this change

The AWS Batch documentation within the CDK library incorrectly stated that the default Spot allocation strategy is `SPOT_CAPACITY_OPTIMIZED`. However, the default was changed to `SPOT_PRICE_CAPACITY_OPTIMIZED` in PR #26731 (August 2023), and several JSDoc `@default` annotations were never updated.

This resulted in inconsistencies between:
- The published CDK API documentation  
- The JSDoc source annotations  
- The actual implementation (`determineAllocationStrategy()`), which correctly uses `SPOT_PRICE_CAPACITY_OPTIMIZED`

This PR updates the documentation to accurately reflect the correct behavior.

### Description of changes

- Updated all incorrect JSDoc `@default` annotations in `managed-compute-environment.ts`.
- Replaced all mentions of `SPOT_CAPACITY_OPTIMIZED` with `SPOT_PRICE_CAPACITY_OPTIMIZED` in affected interfaces and props.
- Ensured consistency across:
  - `IManagedEc2EcsComputeEnvironment`
  - `ManagedEc2EcsComputeEnvironmentProps`
  - `IManagedEc2EksComputeEnvironment`
  - `ManagedEc2EksComputeEnvironmentProps`
- No runtime logic was modified; this PR corrects documentation only.

**Alternatives considered:**
- Leaving the outdated docs in place — rejected because it causes user confusion.
- Introducing a transitional deprecation note — rejected to maintain clean, accurate documentation.

**Design decisions:**
- Align JSDoc documentation with the real default used by the CDK implementation.

### Describe any new or updated permissions being added

No new or updated IAM permissions are introduced.  
This PR updates documentation only.

### Description of how you validated changes

- Verified via code inspection that `determineAllocationStrategy()` already uses the correct default (`SPOT_PRICE_CAPACITY_OPTIMIZED`).
- Searched for all relevant JSDoc `@default` comments and corrected them.
- Rebuilt the module to ensure no JSII or TypeScript documentation inconsistencies.
- Confirmed that no integration tests or runtime behavior are affected.

### Checklist
- [x] My code adheres to the [CONTRIBUTING GUIDE](https://github.com/aws/aws-cdk/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) and [DESIGN GUIDELINES](https://github.com/aws/aws-cdk/blob/main/docs/DESIGN_GUIDELINES.md)

## Summary

- Add `space/invite-ack` message kind so gateways can respond to invitations with credentials sent only to the inviter (not broadcast)
- Implement `space/invite` handler in gateway that generates secure tokens and stores them in `.mew/tokens/`
- Broadcast `system/presence` with `event: 'invited'` to other participants (without exposing credentials)

## Changes

**Spec** (`spec/protocol/SPEC.md`):
- Added `space/invite-ack` to message kinds list
- Updated `space/invite` section with gateway behavior requirements
- Added new section 3.6.6 documenting `space/invite-ack` format and security requirements

**Types** (`src/types/protocol.ts`, `src/types/index.ts`):
- Added `SPACE_INVITE_ACK` to `MessageKinds`
- Added `SpaceInviteAckPayload` interface

**Gateway** (`src/cli/commands/gateway.ts`):
- HTTP API handler for `space/invite`
- WebSocket handler for `space/invite`
- Token generation and secure storage
- Presence broadcast to other participants

- [ ] Send `space/invite` via WebSocket and verify only inviter receives `space/invite-ack`

## Summary

This PR bridges the gap between edge agent tile uploads (Supabase Storage) and the AI inference service, enabling end-to-end inference on slides uploaded by edge agents.

**Key changes:**
- Add `storage.py` with unified storage abstraction supporting S3 and Supabase backends
- Add `fetch_slide()` method to DataFetcher as primary entry point
- Add OpenSlide support for WSI files (.svs, .tif, .ndpi, etc.)
- Update inference service to use SlideData with tile assembly support
- Add comprehensive tests for storage module (25 new tests)
- Update existing inference tests for new fetch_slide API

**Storage backend detection:**
- Explicit: `supabase://` prefix → Supabase Storage
- Auto-detect: `/tiles/` in path → Supabase (when `NT_SUPABASE_AUTODETECT_TILES=true`)
- Default: S3 (legacy/direct uploads)

**Security features:**
- PHI-safe logging with hashed storage IDs
- Size limits (2MB per tile, 10K tiles max)
- Path traversal prevention
- HIPAA-compliant audit logging
- Concurrent tile downloads with semaphore-controlled parallelism

## Test plan

- [x] All 25 storage tests pass
- [x] All 30 inference tests pass
- [x] Ruff linting passes
- [x] Mypy type checking passes
- [x] Black/isort formatting applied
- [ ] Manual integration test with edge agent uploads

- `src/app/services/storage.py` (NEW) - Unified storage abstraction
- `src/app/services/data_fetcher.py` - Added fetch_slide(), OpenSlide support
- `src/app/services/inference.py` - Updated to use SlideData
- `src/app/core/config.py` - Added supabase_autodetect_tiles setting
- `pyproject.toml` - Added openslide-python dependency
- `src/tests/test_storage.py` (NEW) - Storage tests

body:
The TaskTracker CLI had only a placeholder `--file` option and no help system. Replaced it with a complete task management system.

## Changes

### Help System
- Added `help` command with comprehensive usage information
- Supports `help`, `--help`, `-h`, and no-args invocation
- Shows all commands, options, and practical examples

### Task Management Commands
- `add <description>` - Creates tasks with auto-incrementing IDs
- `update <id> <description>` - Modifies task descriptions
- `delete <id>` - Removes tasks
- `mark-in-progress <id>` / `mark-done <id>` - Updates task status
- `list [--status <status>]` - Shows all tasks or filters by status (todo/in-progress/done)

### Data Layer
- JSON-based persistence in `tasks.json`
- Tasks include: ID, description, status, timestamps
- Input validation for empty descriptions

### Configuration
- Added `.gitignore` for build artifacts and data files
- Updated README with usage documentation

## Example Usage

```bash
$ task help
TaskTracker - A CLI app to track tasks and manage your to-do list

Usage:
  task <command> [arguments] [options]

Commands:
  add <description>              Add a new task
  list [--status <status>]       List all tasks or filter by status
  ...

$ task add "Implement feature X"
Task added successfully (ID: 1)

[1] Implement feature X - Status: todo
```

author: ns-rse
body:
- Adds `doi2bibtex` a Bash script that converts DOIs to BibTeX citations. It will accept as input...
  - Accept a single doi with `-d https://doi.org/<doi>`.
  - A file listing multiple DOIs, each on a separate line with `-f doi_file`.
  - Both a `-d` and `-f` argument in which case they are combined.
  - Nothing...in which case the `README.md` is parsed using `grep` and `awk` and the last field of rows that contain `doi` (case-sensitive) are assumed to be the URL for DOIs (based on requested formatting).
- Includes `references.bib`, the result of running `doi2bibtex` on the current `README.md`
- Updates the `README.md` with instructions on usage and a couple of other minor changes, mainly formatting.
- Adds @ns-rse to `AUTHORS.md`

Short-comings/things to consider

Providing a Bash script _and_ instructions suggesting `references.bib` should be updated when adding entries assumes users have access to a Bash shell which may not always be the case. Possible solutions considered...

- Implement in Python and/or R.
- Add a GitHub Action to auto-generate `references.bib` on merges and remove request for users to generate and include in the commit.

The later would be my preference as it automates the process and removes a burden/barrier for contributors. I will create an issue and undertake this work.

body:
## Fix screeps-graphite-exporter console subscription spam

### Problem
The exporter was logging "Subscribed to console events" repeatedly every ~3 seconds and stats were never being pushed to Graphite.

### Root Cause
The code was registering TWO event handlers for console events:
1. `socket.on('console', callback)` - direct event listener
2. `socket.subscribe('console', callback)` - which internally calls `this.on(path, cb)` to register another event listener

This duplicate registration caused both handlers to fire on every console event, creating conflicts and preventing proper message processing.

### Solution
- [x] Analyze the issue and understand the root cause
- [x] Remove duplicate handler registration
- [x] Use only `socket.subscribe('console', callback)` which properly registers the event handler
- [x] Add log message only on first message received to confirm subscription is working
- [x] Build and verify the fix compiles
- [x] Fix code review feedback (trailing whitespace)
- [x] Run code review
- [x] Run security checks (0 alerts found)
- [x] Complete the task

### Changes Made
- **packages/screeps-graphite-exporter/src/consoleListener.ts**:
  - Removed duplicate `socket.on('console', ...)` event handler
  - Kept only `socket.subscribe('console', callback)` which properly handles console events
  - Added first-message-only logging to confirm subscription is working without spam
  - Fixed trailing whitespace

### Expected Behavior After Fix
- "Subscribed to console events and receiving messages" logged only ONCE when first console message is received
- Console messages processed correctly
- Stats properly pushed to Grafana Cloud Graphite
- Log messages like "Sent X metrics to Grafana Cloud Graphite" should appear

## Security Summary
No security vulnerabilities found in the changes.

- [x] Update observation space to include rich feature channels (row/col fill %, holes, valid placements)
- [x] Revamp reward system with strategic shaping (hole penalties, fragmentation penalties, line completion bonuses, survival bonus)

<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

# Problem

The current BlockBlast AI performs poorly due to several fundamental issues in the architecture, reward system, and observation space. This PR should address all of them comprehensively.

## Issues to Fix

### 1. Observation Space is Too Simplistic
**Current:** Raw binary grids only (grid + hand)

**Required Fix:** Add rich feature channels to help the network understand the game state:
- Channel for row fill percentages (how close each row is to being cleared)
- Channel for column fill percentages
- Channel for hole/unreachable cell detection
- Channel showing valid placement positions for current pieces
- Normalize all observations properly

### 2. Wrong Network Architecture (MLP instead of CNN)
**Current:** Fully-connected layers `[1024, 512, 256]` that treat the grid as a flat vector

**Required Fix:** Implement a custom CNN feature extractor:
- Use convolutional layers to detect spatial patterns (near-complete lines, holes, clusters)
- Proper architecture: Conv2D layers with increasing filters (32 → 64 → 128)
- Batch normalization for training stability
- Combine grid features with hand features appropriately
- Output to smaller fully-connected layers for policy/value heads

### 3. Poor Reward Shaping
**Current rewards:**
- `+1 to +9` for placing blocks (encourages random filling)
- `-50` for game over (too weak)
- `+5` for refilling hand
- No penalty for creating holes or fragmentation

**Required Fix:** Implement strategic reward shaping:
```python
# Remove or reduce reward for just placing blocks
# Add hole penalty: -1.0 * number_of_holes created
# Add fragmentation penalty: penalize isolated empty cells
# Add near-complete line bonus: +0.5 for each row/col with 7/8 cells filled
# Increase game-over penalty to -200 or scale based on how early game ended
# Add survival bonus: small positive reward for each step survived
# Bonus for keeping the board "open" (connectivity metric)
```

### 4. Guaranteed-Valid Piece Refill Removes Learning Pressure
**Current:** `_refill_hand()` only gives pieces that can definitely be placed

**Required Fix:** 
- Make piece selection random (true to the real game)
- OR use a probability-based system (e.g., 80% random, 20% guaranteed valid)
- This forces the AI to learn to keep space available for any piece type

### 5. Hyperparameter Tuning
**Current issues:**
- `ent_coef=0.01` is too low for 192 actions
- Training may be insufficient

**Required Fix:**
- Increase `ent_coef` to 0.02-0.05 for better exploration
- Add learning rate scheduling (start higher, decay over time)
- Consider adding gradient clipping adjustments
- Add proper evaluation callbacks to track real performance

### 6. Additional Improvements Needed

**Add helper functions for reward calculation:**
- `count_holes(grid)`: Count cells that are empty but unreachable from top
- `count_near_complete_lines(grid)`: Count rows/cols with 6+ cells filled
- `calculate_fragmentation(grid)`: Measure how scattered empty cells are
- `calculate_surface_roughness(grid)`: Penalize uneven column heights

**Improve the training script:**
- Add evaluation callback that runs episodes without exploration
- Log more metrics: average episode length, holes created, lines cleared
- Save best model based on evaluation score, not just checkpoints

**Update the observation space definition:**
```python
self.observation_space = spaces.Dict({
    "grid": spaces.Box(low=0, high=1, shape=(num_channels, grid_size, grid_size), dtype=np.float32),
    "hand": spaces.Box(low=0, high=1, shape=(3, max_block_size, max_block_size), dtype=np.float32)
})
```

## Files to Modify

1. **block_blast_env.py**: 
   - Rewrite observation space with multiple channels
   - Add all helper metric functions (holes, fragmentation, etc.)
   - Completely revamp the reward function in `step()`
   - Modify `_refill_hand()` to use random pieces
   - Add Numba-optimized versions of new metric functions

2. **train.py**:
   - Create custom CNN feature extractor class
   - Update policy_kwargs to use the CNN
   - Adjust hyperparameters (ent_coef, learning rate schedule)
   - Add evaluation callback
   - Increase default timesteps recommendation

3. **Create new file `feature_extractor.py`** (optional, or include in train.py):
   - Custom CNN class inheriting from BaseFeaturesExtractor
   - Proper handling of Dict observation space

## Expected Outcome

After these changes, the AI should:
- Learn to clear lines strategically
- Avoid creating holes and fragmented spaces
- Plan ahead to keep the board playable
- Achieve significantly higher scores and longer games
- Show clear learning progress in TensorBoard metrics

## Technical Requirements

- Maintain compatibility with sb3_contrib MaskablePPO
- Keep Numba optimizations for performance-critical functions
- Ensure observation space changes work with the action masking system
- All new code should follow existing code style (French comments are fine)

author: codyebberson
body:
There were actually two bugs here:

1. If the bot threw an error, the custom operation handler tried to send the return value (i.e., the error `OperationOutcome`) through `buildOutputParameters()`, which wouldn't make any sense, and which caused errors.
2. If `buildOutputParameters()` throws (which can happen for many other reasons), that error was unhandled, which caused a 500.

So the respective fixes:

1. If the bot threw (i.e., `botResult.success === false`), then don't call `buildOutputParameters()`
2. Wrap the call to `buildOutputParameters()` in `try`/`catch`, and return a more helpful error message if it fails

author: whitwaldo
body:
# Description

This PR represents an effort to dramatically overhaul how the .NET implementation of Dapr Workflows is written.

This completely removes our dependency on the DurableTask libraries (including our fork of [Dapr.DurableTask](https://github.com/dapr/durabletask-dotnet)) and fundamentally alters how the underlying system works operationally to remove all the logic not directly used by the Dapr runtime, applies modern .NET architecture ideas and syntax (nullability support, DI, records) and most of all, seeks to avoid any breaking changes with the existing Dapr.Workflow public API.

This approach simplifies the gRPC client creation to eliminate several types of bugs seen in the development of 1.16 and to further improve reliability and performance of the client, especially during heavy load.

Updating the examples, the only change needed was that requests to get the workflow state return a nullable instance of `WorkflowState`, but I otherwise saw drop-in support.

Outside of just making it easier to develop and maintain the project, this implementation also fixes several issues raised by the broader community:

#1567 identified issues with Serilog registration because of the additional scope creation as part of the DI registration - because the underlying types are registered differently, the additional scope creation has been removed and this issue will be resolved.

#1537 and #1582 sought more customized workflow serialization support. I'll do you one better - this implementation completely abstracts all serialization into an `IWorkflowSerializer` and provides a default implementation using System.Text.Json. Via the DI registration methods, you can pass in your own `JsonSerializationOptions` or even implement your own concrete serializer (just needs to be able to serialize/deserialize to and from a string) to support MessagePack, BSON or whatever you want and it'll just work. Do use some caution here - changing any of these settings means that when a workflow is rehydrated, it may not deserialize properly and would throw instead of complete successfully. Further, if you're using multi-app run (not yet supported in .NET, but WIP), your other applications will need to similarly support the same serialization scheme - to my knowledge, all other Dapr SDKs support JSON exclusively, so be advised.

#1532 calls to making it easier to demonstrate testing workflows, so I've added several interfaces throughout that can be used to facilitate this.

I've added support for task execution IDs per #1541 and am working on multi-app run per #1636 along with a bunch of unit tests to validate it through.

No changes should be necessary to the documentation as it should be a drop-in replacement for the existing public API, even though the entire backing apparatus has changed.

We strive to have all PR being opened based on an issue, where the problem or feature have been discussed prior to implementation.

author: leonelramirez
body:
Hi @alexdryden, following up on our discussion regarding optimization of the full re-indexing process (#3 and UIUCLibrary/arcuit#39), I implemented some enhancements that reduced processing time to approximately 30% of the original sequential approach:
- Introduced multithreading to leverage concurrent processing where applicable.
- Incorporated classification data (recordgroup and subgroup) into the XML file. 
- Executed the `traject` command directly (instead of `arcuit:index` or `arclight:index`) with parameter adjustments to enable efficient batched processing.

With these enhancements we only need this modified version of [ead_from_aspace_classifications.rb](https://github.com/UIUCLibrary/arcuit/blob/ac505edd222e97f7693cac7c950e0f3aef341629/lib/arcuit/traject/ead_from_aspace_classifications.rb) on Arcuit's side to process the additional classification data in the XML. 

A single cron job on the server continues to manage both full re-indexing and individual record updates.

Despite the overall time improvements, the PDF generation remains the primary bottleneck in the process. I'm still reviewing whether we can introduce concurrency (via our ASpace plugin) for the background jobs that generate the PDFs in ASpace.

author: chesars
body:
## Title

fix(anthropic): capture web_search_tool_result in streaming for multi-turn conversations

## Relevant issues

Fixes #17737 for streaming with Anthropic web search tool

## Pre-Submission checklist

- [x] I have Added testing in the [`tests/litellm/`](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/tree/main/tests/litellm) directory, **Adding at least 1 test is a hard requirement**
- [x] I have added a screenshot of my new test passing locally 
- [x] My PR passes all unit tests on [`make test-unit`](https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/extras/contributing_code)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible, it only solves 1 specific problem

## Type

🐛 Bug Fix

## Changes

This fix addresses two issues with Anthropic web search streaming:

### 1. Fix trailing `{}` in tool call arguments

`web_search_tool_result` blocks have `input_json_delta` that were emitted as tool calls, with invalid JSON like:
```
arguments = '{"query": "fun otter facts"}{}{}{}'  ❌
```

**Fix:** Added `current_content_block_type` tracking to only emit tool calls for `tool_use` and `server_tool_use` blocks.

### 2. Capture `web_search_tool_result` in streaming

**Request:**
```python
response = completion(
    model="anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-20250514",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Search the web for weather in Tokyo"}],
    stream=True,
    tools=[{"type": "web_search_20250305", "name": "web_search", "max_uses": 1}]
)
```

**Anthropic sends (streaming SSE):**
```
event: content_block_start
data: {"type": "content_block_start", "content_block": {"type": "server_tool_use", "id": "srvtoolu_01ABC", "name": "web_search"}}

event: content_block_start  
data: {"type": "content_block_start", "content_block": {"type": "web_search_tool_result", "tool_use_id": "srvtoolu_01ABC", "content": [{"url": "...", "title": "...", "encrypted_content": "..."}]}}
```

**Before fix:** `web_search_tool_result` was ignored → `provider_specific_fields.web_search_results` was empty → multi-turn failed

**After fix:** LiteLLM returns:
```python
{
  "choices": [{
    "delta": {
      "tool_calls": [{"id": "srvtoolu_01ABC", "function": {"name": "web_search", "arguments": "{...}"}}],
      "provider_specific_fields": {
        "web_search_results": [{"type": "web_search_tool_result", "tool_use_id": "srvtoolu_01ABC", "content": [...]}]
      }
    }
  }]
}
```

Now multi-turn works because `stream_chunk_builder` preserves `provider_specific_fields` .

### Tests added

### Files changed

- `litellm/llms/anthropic/chat/handler.py` - Streaming handler fixes
- `litellm/main.py` - `stream_chunk_builder` provider_specific_fields handling
- `tests/test_litellm/llms/anthropic/chat/test_anthropic_chat_handler.py` - 3 new tests

body:
The action fails when the `gh_pages` branch doesn't exist remotely, with error `cd: gh_pages: No such file or directory` at line 315.

## Root Cause

The orphan branch creation step incorrectly creates a local subdirectory, changes into it, then attempts git operations:

```bash
mkdir -p gh_pages
cd gh_pages
git switch --orphan gh_pages  # Wrong: creates branch inside subdirectory
```

The next step deletes this directory, but when checkout falls back to `main` (branch doesn't exist), the subsequent `cd "${GH_PAGES}"` fails.

## Changes

**Fixed orphan branch creation** (action.yml:147-186)
- Removed directory creation/navigation; orphan branch now created at repository root
- Added branch restoration: `git checkout "${CURRENT_BRANCH}"` after orphan branch push
- Use parameterized `"${{ inputs.gh_pages }}"` instead of hardcoded `"gh_pages"`

**Security hardening**
- Quoted all `${{ inputs.gh_pages }}` references (lines 163, 168, 172, 267, 271)
- Quoted environment variables `$GIT_USER_EMAIL` and `$GIT_USER_NAME` (lines 265-266)

```bash
# Before
mkdir -p gh_pages
cd gh_pages
git switch --orphan gh_pages

# After
git switch --orphan "${{ inputs.gh_pages }}"
git push -u origin "${{ inputs.gh_pages }}"
git checkout "${CURRENT_BRANCH}"
```

author: copilot
body:
Input and textarea fields in the worksheet editor lose focus while typing, forcing users to re-click after each character. This occurs because `layout` prop on parent `motion.div` elements triggers full layout recalculations (position + size) on every debounced update (300ms), causing focus interruption.

## Changes

Changed `layout` to `layout="position"` on motion.div wrappers to restrict animations to position-only:

- **task-item.tsx**: Main task container
- **task-list.tsx**: List containers wrapping task items  
- **task-notes.tsx**: Note editing sections

```tsx
// Before: triggers full layout animation including size
<motion.div layout className="...">
  <Input {...field} />
</motion.div>

// After: only animates position, preserves input focus
<motion.div layout="position" className="...">
  <Input {...field} />
</motion.div>
```

This preserves drag-and-drop position animations while preventing size-based recalculations that interfere with input focus.

body:
Adds support for `#include` preprocessor directives, enabling symbol resolution, go-to-definition, and find-references across included shader files.

### Core Changes

- **Include resolver** (`src/includeResolver.ts`): Parses `#include "..."` and `#include <...>` directives, resolves paths relative to current file and configurable search paths, handles nested includes (max 10 depth), prevents circular references

- **Include definition provider**: Ctrl+click on include paths opens the included file

- **Symbol/definition/reference providers updated**: Now search included files for symbols when not found in current document

- **GLSL semantic provider**: Extracts struct names from includes for semantic highlighting

### Configuration

New setting `shader.includePaths` for additional search directories:

```json
{
    "shader.includePaths": [
        "shaders/include",
        "/absolute/path/to/includes"
    ]
}
```

### Search Order

- Local includes (`"..."`) → current file directory → configured paths → workspace roots
- System includes (`<...>`) → configured paths → workspace roots → current file directory

author: benface
body:
## Summary

- Add explicit `.js` file extensions to all relative imports across the `common`, `core`, and `react` packages
- Update build scripts to generate `.js` extensions in generated files
- Use `import type` for type-only imports per ESLint rules

## Problem

Projects using TypeScript's `moduleResolution: "NodeNext"` or `"Node16"` (strict ESM resolution) fail to resolve types from `@web3icons/react` and other packages. The compiled `.d.ts` files contain extensionless imports like:

```typescript
export * from './icons'
```

Under strict ESM module resolution, these fail because Node.js requires explicit file extensions for ESM imports.

## Solution

Add `.js` extensions to all relative imports in source files. TypeScript compiles these to `.d.ts` files that work with both bundler-style and Node.js-style module resolution:

```typescript
export * from './icons/index.js'
```

## Test plan

- [x] `bun build:packages` succeeds
- [x] `bun format` passes
- [x] Tested with a project using `moduleResolution: "NodeNext"` - TypeScript types now resolve correctly

author: krystophny
body:
## Summary

Enforces FORTRAN 66 (ANSI X3.9-1966 Section 7.1.2.4) restrictions on logical IF statement bodies. The logical IF statement must not contain:
- Another logical IF statement (no nesting)
- A DO statement  
- Any non-executable statement (DIMENSION, COMMON, FORMAT, etc.)

## Changes

**Grammar:** `grammars/src/FORTRAN66Parser.g4`
- Created new `logical_if_body` rule with explicit allowed executable statements
- Updated `logical_if_stmt` to use `logical_if_body` instead of generic `statement_body`
- Added comprehensive comments documenting X3.9-1966 Section 7.1.2.4 restrictions

**Tests:** `tests/FORTRAN66/test_fortran66_parser.py`
- `test_logical_if_valid_statements`: 8 valid executable statement cases
- `test_logical_if_invalid_nested_if`: 2 cases rejecting nested logical IF (parser should fail)
- `test_logical_if_invalid_do_statement`: 2 cases rejecting DO statement in IF (parser should fail)

## Verification

```bash
make test
# Result: 1374 passed, 1 skipped in 26.09s ✓
```

All existing tests pass with no regressions. New tests verify that invalid statements are correctly rejected by the parser.

## Standards Compliance

**STANDARD-COMPLIANT** with ISO/IEC 1539 (ANSI X3.9-1966) Section 7.1.2.4:
- Implements full grammatical enforcement of logical IF body restrictions
- Prevents nesting of logical IF statements
- Rejects DO statements in logical IF bodies
- Rejects non-executable statements in logical IF bodies

## Closes

Fixes #397

author: drvegabermudez
body:
Modernize CMake for macOS ARM: raise minimum versions, quiet policies/Boost, add arm64 EPICS host/target detection, map AppleClang→clang, and wire EPICS compiler/os include paths.

Enable EPICS/PVA and OpenMP: configure TRY_EPICS, remove unused Boost components, set Homebrew libomp paths, and propagate OpenMP includes.

Fix Python integration: switch flame/pyconfig.py to sysconfig (distutils-free), skip nose on Python ≥3.12, add thor shim package and math re-export, and ensure Python extensions build against the installed prefix.

Resolve build blockers: add missing headers, remove unused GSL includes, add override specifiers, correct multipole defaults (B_n/K) and main multipole numbers for bend/sextupole; C++ ctest now passes 34/34.

Docs and install: expand macOS ARM64 README quickstart with full CMake configure line; install artifacts to install/ prefix; build and install gtpsa and thor_scsi Python wheels.

Note remaining Python test gaps: some tests reference a missing external lattice file, expect unexported constants, rely on an unshipped _gtpsa_variant_test, and hit placeholder utilities (jac_intern_to_std, Matrix binding); these need follow-up or test adjustments.

body:
Add hands-free, always-on, wake-word driven conversational system:

New modules:
- WakeLoopEngine.ts: Continuous polling loop (~150ms) for wake-word detection
  - 8-state state machine (idle -> listening -> wake_detected -> capturing -> processing -> speaking -> resetting -> idle)
  - 3 power modes (active, power_saving, suspended)
  - Audio context dropout recovery
  - Dependency injection for external handlers

- WakeWordSensitivityController.ts: Dynamic sensitivity tuning
  - High/Medium/Low sensitivity presets
  - Auto-adjust on false positives
  - Auto-boost on missed wakes
  - STT confidence scoring fallback

- NoiseSuppressionEngine.ts: WebAudio noise reduction
  - High-pass/low-pass/notch filters
  - Voice Activity Detection (VAD) with smoothing
  - Auto-gain control
  - Real-time audio monitoring

- ContinuousListeningController.ts: Master controller
  - Orchestrates all Phase 4 components
  - Interruption detection during TTS
  - State management and callbacks

- HandsFreeModeManager.ts: Toggle and persistence
  - localStorage preference storage
  - Auto-start on load option
  - Session tracking and statistics

- MicEngineHooks.ts: Hook layer for MicEngine
  - onWakeTriggered, onSpeechStart, onSpeechEnd, onAutoReset hooks
  - Audio level monitoring
  - Speech duration validation

- ContinuousListeningIndicator.tsx: UI indicator component
  - Pulsing orb with state-based colors
  - Particle animation on wake detection
  - Three variants (default, compact, floating)

Integration:
- CopilotOrchestrator.ts updated with Phase 4 methods
  - initializeContinuousListening()
  - startContinuousListening()
  - stopContinuousListening()
  - toggleContinuousListening()
  - getContinuousListeningState()

All modules are fully isolated - no existing logic modified.

body:
When profiling code it's often valuable to understand what
code paths are executing while exceptions are being handled. The new
--mode=exception option filters samples to only include threads that
have an active exception, making it easy to identify hot spots in error
handling code without noise from normal execution paths.

This works by checking both the thread's current_exception (for
exceptions being raised/propagated) and exc_info (for exceptions being
handled in except blocks). The feature integrates with the existing
profiler infrastructure including the live TUI, flamegraph output, and
gecko format for Firefox Profiler visualization.

author: nvp-stripe
body:
## Fix Inconsistency in OpenAPI Spec

1. In json schema (spec/json-schema/schema.agentic_checkout.json)
In the json schema file, the `FulfillmentOptionShipping` has:
```
"subtotal": {
  "type": "integer"
},
"tax": {
  "type": "integer"
},
"total": {
  "type": "integer"
}
```

2. OpenAPI Spec (spec/openapi/openapi.agentic_checkout.yaml)
The OpenAPI file `FulfillmentOptionShipping` had these types as strings:
```
subtotal: { type: string }
tax: { type: string }
total: { type: string }
```

3. RFC documentation (rfcs/rfc.agentic_checkout.md)
> "All endpoints MUST use HTTPS and return JSON. Amounts MUST be integers in minor units."

and in Section 5 (Data Model (authoritative extract)) of the RFC explicitly states:

> "FulfillmentOption (shipping): type: "shipping", id, title, subtitle?, carrier?, earliest_delivery_time?, latest_delivery_time?, subtotal?, tax?, total (int)"

Note the int at the end indicating all money amounts are integers.

4. Examples file (examples/examples.agentic_checkout.json)
In the examples, these fields are consistently shown as numbers (not quoted strings):
```
"subtotal": 100,
"tax": 0,
"total": 100
```

**Fixed OpenAPI spec** (`spec/openapi/openapi.agentic_checkout.yaml`):
   - Changed `subtotal` from `type: string` to `type: integer` in `FulfillmentOptionShipping`
   - Changed `tax` from `type: string` to `type: integer` in `FulfillmentOptionShipping`
   - Changed `total` from `type: string` to `type: integer` in `FulfillmentOptionShipping`
   - Changed `subtotal` from `type: string` to `type: integer` in `FulfillmentOptionDigital`
   - Changed `tax` from `type: string` to `type: integer` in `FulfillmentOptionDigital`
   - Changed `total` from `type: string` to `type: integer` in `FulfillmentOptionDigital`

**Changelog**
Added entry documenting this as a bug fix/clarification
Explained the inconsistency and impact

**Compatibility**
The RFC has always required integer amounts, and all examples demonstrate integer usage
Implementations following the RFC should already be using integers
This aligns the OpenAPI schema with actual specification behavior

author: alesevero
body:
_Note: branched off of #596_

## Description

Improves the ergonomics when using the new decorators with responses coming out of the Sanity typescript clients, by making SanityResponse a _mappable_ data structure.

The benefits of this change goes beyond decorators. As the sanity response holds data that we can apply functions to, data manipulation becomes a trivial function composition using `.map()`. This is a step forward into being able to extract complex sanity data manipulation logic into smaller, composable building blocks, allowing more flexibility and type-safety when handling sanity responses.

**Before:**
```typescript
// Manual decorator application with mutation
let res = await contentClient.fetchList<Lesson>(q, {
  sort,
  offset,
  limit,
})

res = pageTypeDecorator(needsAccessDecorator(res, userPermissions, adapter))
return res
```

**After:**
```typescript
// Clean functional composition
return (await contentClient.fetchList<Lesson>(q, {...}))
  .map(needsAccessDecorator(perms, adapter))
  .map(pageTypeDecorator)
```

Fully type safe: the snippet above returns `SanityListResponse<Lesson & NeedAccessDecorated & PageTypeDecorated>`

### **Core Infrastructure Changes**

- **`SanityResponse<T>` & `SanityListResponse<T>` now implement `Functor<T>`**
  - Converted from interfaces to classes with `.map()` method
  - Immutable transformations - each `.map()` returns a new instance
  - Full type safety with covariant return types
  - Located in: `src/infrastructure/sanity/interfaces/SanityResponse.ts`

- **Refactored Decorators to be Immutable & Curried**
  - `pageTypeDecorator`: Pure function that adds `page_type` field ('song' or 'lesson')
  - `needsAccessDecorator`: Curried function `(perms, adapter) => (content) => decorated`
  - `contentDecorator`: Core traversal function for nested `content[]` and `lessons[]` arrays

## Future Enhancements

Potential follow-ups (not in this PR):
- Support asynchronous decorators
- Add more decorators following the same pattern
- Consider Applicative/Monad if use cases emerge
- Extract decorator composition utilities if patterns emerge

## Description

This pull request introduces comprehensive support for field and column mapping within the `rhosocial-activerecord-postgres` backend. It includes implementation for annotated type adapters and direct backend tests, ensuring that custom column names and type conversions work seamlessly with PostgreSQL.

## Related Issues

<!--
List any issues that this PR closes or is dependent on.
For example: Closes #123, Fixes #456, Relates to #789.
-->

## Proposed Changes

- **Full Support for Mapped Column Models**: Enables the use of custom column names for model fields in PostgreSQL backend, allowing for flexible mapping between Python object fields and database column names.
- **Annotated Type Adapter Support**: Implements the necessary infrastructure and specific PostgreSQL provider for `Annotated` type adapters, ensuring proper data conversion and validation for fields with custom types.
- **Enhanced Test Coverage**:
    - Added column mapping tests and updated dependencies.
    - Included new test cases for field and column mapping to cover various scenarios.
- **Adjusted Schema for Timezone-Aware Datetime**: Modified the test schema to correctly handle timezone-aware datetime values, ensuring accurate and consistent data processing.

body:
Three issues: score/rating overflows QC box on mobile, toggles render as circles on mobile, and rerunning analysis with existing images fails with `atob()` error.

## Changes

### Mobile responsive layout for QC report cards
- Header now stacks vertically on mobile (`flex-col md:flex-row`)
- Responsive text sizing for scores (`text-lg md:text-xl`)
- Reduced padding on mobile viewports (`px-2 md:px-3`)

### Toggle component aspect ratio preservation
- Added `min-w-[2.75rem]` constraint to button element
- Prevents toggle from shrinking into circular shape on small screens

### Fix image reprocessing error
Root cause: `rerunQCWithExistingImages` passed public URLs to `db.saveImage()`, which expects base64 data URLs. The `atob()` decoder fails on URL strings.

```typescript
// Before: passed URLs directly
const previousQCImages = currentReport.qcImageIds.map(id => getPublicImageUrl(user.id, id));

// After: fetch actual base64 data
const previousQCImages = await Promise.all(
  currentReport.qcImageIds.map(async (id) => {
    const base64Data = await db.getImage(id);
    if (!base64Data) {
      // Fallback: fetch from URL and convert
      const response = await fetch(getPublicImageUrl(user.id, id));
      const blob = await response.blob();
      return blobToDataURL(blob);
    }
    return base64Data;
  })
);
```

author: kaspro-coder
body:
## What
This PR implements the full end-to-end flow for the **“What did I miss?”** feature.

The system now:
- Detects course-related queries using a Regex-based intent detector.
- Performs an on-demand Moodle scrape when a course or week is identified.
- Returns structured JSON (`type: "moodle_overview"`) with cleaned Markdown and metadata.
- Renders results natively on Android, including a Moodle-styled badge.

This provides a deterministic and reliable pipeline for retrieving course summaries.

---

## How
- Added `detectCourseIntent` to intercept eligible queries before they reach the LLM.
- Implemented `getCourseOverview` to scrape Moodle when the cache is older than 4 hours.
- Added fallback logic to select the most recent non-empty section when the requested week has no content.
- Refactored `moodleParser` to remove HTML tags, strip file lists, and shorten long descriptions.
- Updated the Android client to support the `moodle_overview` payload:
  - Added `MoodleBadge.kt`.
  - Updated Chat UI rendering logic.
  - Added `kotlinx.serialization` models for structured parsing.

File changes include:
- New intent-detection utility.
- New scraping and caching logic.
- Updated Android models and UI components.

---

## Why
Previously, “What did I miss?” queries relied on generic LLM generation, leading to inconsistent results.

This PR is necessary because:
- The feature requires deterministic intent detection rather than probabilistic generation.
- Moodle content must be fetched in real time for specific weeks or courses.
- The Android app needs structured data for native rendering.
- Direct scraping ensures accuracy and freshness of course summaries.
- This unlocks future improvements such as multi-week overviews and better caching.

This PR delivers the first fully functional and deterministic implementation of the “What did I miss?” feature.

closes #246

The optimizer lacked visual output for schedules and cashflows, making it hard to see timing, cumulative spend/benefit, and annual funding vs. net balance.

- **Visualization module**: Helpers to build benefit profiles and render program schedule Gantt, cumulative spend/benefit, and annual spend/net/funding plots; matplotlib added as a dependency.

- **Robustness/docs**: Case-insensitive dimension lookup, logging for invalid/missing start years, clarified docstrings; focused tests for benefit alignment and file-driven visualization.

from pathlib import Path

body: This PR adjusts the formula for calculating the color of buttons on hover and when active. author: pierrevieira
body:
This commit refactors the reading plan and day features to improve module separation and decouple the progress calculation logic.

The key changes are:
-   **Introduced `CalculateBibleProgressUseCase`**: A new use case in the `core/books` module is added to calculate the overall Bible reading progress based on all verses.
-   **Decoupled Progress Calculation**: The `ReadingPlanViewModel` now uses `CalculateBibleProgressUseCase` for progress tracking, removing the plan-specific calculation logic and ensuring a consistent progress value across the app.
-   **Moved Domain Logic**: `DayRepository` and `UpdateDayReadStatusUseCase` have been moved from the `feature/day` module to the `core/plan` module. This improves the domain structure by placing shared plan-related logic in the core module.
-   **Simplified ViewModel**: `ReadingPlanViewModel` is updated to delegate day status updates to the moved `UpdateDayReadStatusUseCase` and to consume the new `CalculateBibleProgressUseCase` for progress updates.

Other changes include:
-   **CI**: A new Python script (`fix_file_endings.py`) is added to enforce consistent file endings.
-   **Build**: The application version is incremented to `1.0.1`.
-   **Style**: Trailing whitespace has been removed from numerous JSON and XML resource files.

author: mldangelo
body:
## Summary

A gift for @jameshiester 🎁

This PR adds a new `promptfoo logs` command that allows users to view, list, and follow log files directly from the CLI, making debugging and troubleshooting significantly easier.

### Features

- **View logs**: Display the most recent or a specific log file with syntax highlighting
- **Tail mode**: Show last N lines with `-n/--lines` option
- **Head mode**: Show first N lines with `--head` option
- **Follow mode**: Real-time log monitoring with `-f/--follow` (like `tail -f`)
- **List logs**: Browse available log files with `--list` or `logs list` subcommand
- **Type filtering**: Filter by log type (`debug`, `error`, or `all`)
- **Fuzzy matching**: Find logs by partial filename or date

### Examples

```sh
# View most recent log
promptfoo logs

# View last 50 lines
promptfoo logs -n 50

# Follow logs in real-time
promptfoo logs -f

# List all log files
promptfoo logs --list

# View specific log by partial match
promptfoo logs 2024-01-15
```

### Implementation

- New `src/commands/logs.ts` - Main command implementation
- New `src/util/logs.ts` - Shared log utilities (extracted from export.ts)
- Updated `src/commands/export.ts` - Now uses shared utilities
- 35 unit tests covering all functionality
- Documentation added to site/docs/usage/command-line.md

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests for log utilities (17 tests)
- [x] Unit tests for logs command (18 tests)
- [x] Manual integration testing:
  - [x] `promptfoo logs --help` displays usage
  - [x] `promptfoo logs --list` shows available logs
  - [x] `promptfoo logs -n 5` shows last 5 lines
  - [x] `promptfoo logs <filename>` displays specific file
  - [x] `promptfoo logs -f` follows in real-time

author: spacecodee
body:
## 🔧 Hotfix: TruffleHog Security Workflow Configuration (0.0.2)

### Issue
TruffleHog was failing on Dependabot PRs and push events with:
```
Error: BASE and HEAD commits are the same. TruffleHog won't scan anything.
```

This prevented security scanning on dependency update PRs and caused CI failures.

### Root Cause
The workflow was using a static base branch comparison (`main`) which caused false positives when:
- Dependabot pushed commits directly
- Feature branches were scanned
- Push events occurred on main branch

### Solution
Implemented context-aware commit detection in TruffleHog configuration:

**Event-specific behavior:**
- **Pull Requests**: Compare against PR base SHA
- **Push (existing branch)**: Compare against previous commit
- **Push (new branch)**: Compare against HEAD~1 for efficiency
- **Scheduled runs**: Scan recent commits only (HEAD~1)
- **Manual triggers**: Scan recent commits only (HEAD~1)

### Changes
- ✅ Added intelligent event detection step
- ✅ Dynamic base/head determination
- ✅ Improved regex-based detection for new branches
- ✅ Enhanced efficiency with HEAD~1 instead of full history scans
- ✅ Better documentation of event handling

### Impact
- ✅ Fixes Dependabot PR scanning (#14, #15, #16)
- ✅ Enables feature branch security scanning
- ✅ Improves CI/CD reliability
- ✅ Reduces unnecessary full-repository scans

### Testing
- PR #17 was merged to develop and passed CI
- Ready for production release

**Type of change:** Bug Fix / Hotfix  
**Semantic Version:** 0.0.1 → 0.0.2 (PATCH)

body:
ソート機能はほぼ使用されず、完了済みタスクを期日の近い順で見ると古いタスクから表示されて不便。手動ソート機能を廃止し、フィルタータイプに応じて自動ソートを実装。

## Changes

### Filter & Sort Logic
- **Removed**: Manual sort controls (`SortType`, sort dropdown UI)
- **Removed**: "all" filter option (unused)
- **Changed**: Default filter from "all" → "active"
- **Added**: Auto-sort based on filter type:
  - `active`: ascending by date (earliest deadline first)
  - `completed`: descending by date (most recent first)

### Implementation

**`filterAtom.ts`**
```typescript
// Before
export type FilterType = "all" | "active" | "completed";
export type SortType = "date-asc" | "date-desc";
const filterAtom = atomWithStorage<FilterType>("todo-filter", "all");
const sortAtom = atomWithStorage<SortType>("todo-sort", "date-asc");

// After
export type FilterType = "active" | "completed";
const filterAtom = atomWithStorage<FilterType>("todo-filter", "active");
```

**`useGroupedTodos.ts`**
```typescript
const getSortCompareFunction = (filter: string) => {
  if (filter === "completed") {
    return (a: Todo, b: Todo) => b.endAt - a.endAt; // 降順
  }
  return (a: Todo, b: Todo) => a.endAt - b.endAt; // 昇順
};
```

### UI Changes

**Before**: 3 filter buttons + sort dropdown
![before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/33b1ccab-417d-431a-ad4e-fcc22a0d7348)

**After - Active tasks** (early dates first):
![active](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/405cc649-f4b6-40b4-be51-ba576522e6da)

**After - Completed tasks** (recent dates first):
![completed](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4d1153c0-2d17-40cb-a57d-be1ad65c0074)

### Testing
Added in-source tests for sort comparison functions covering ascending/descending order and edge cases (tasks without dates).

author: gadievron
body:
## Summary

This PR replaces individual LLM provider implementations with a unified LiteLLM integration, providing:
- Automatic fallback across multiple LLM providers
- Unified cost tracking and budget limits  
- Retry logic with exponential backoff
- Response caching
- Task-specific model selection

## All Cursor Bot Bugs Fixed ✅

This PR includes fixes for **all 5 Cursor bot bugs** identified in the original review:

### Bug #1 (HIGH): Tuple Unpacking in fuzzer.py:109
- **Issue**: `generate_structured()` returns `(Dict, str)` tuple, but code wasn't unpacking it
- **Fix**: Changed `result = ...` to `result, _ = ...`
- **Impact**: Prevents runtime errors

### Bug #2 (HIGH): API Key Sanitization in client.py:289,296
- **Issue**: Exception messages logged without sanitization, potential API key leakage
- **Fix**: Added `_sanitize_log_message()` wrapper to exception logging
- **Documentation**: Enhanced with searchable tags (#SECURITY, #API_KEY_PROTECTION)
- **Rationale**: Defense-in-depth (LiteLLM sanitizes its logs, we sanitize ours)
- **Impact**: Prevents API key leakage in application logs

### Bug #3 (MEDIUM): Exploitability Check in agent.py:1047-1058
- **Issue**: `generate_patch()` was being called for all vulnerabilities
- **Fix**: Wrapped patch generation in `if vuln.exploitable:` guard
- **Impact**: Prevents unnecessary patch generation for non-exploitable vulns

### Bug #4 (MEDIUM): Ollama api_base Configuration in providers.py:235-237
- **Issue**: `api_base` configuration not being passed to LiteLLM
- **Fix**: Added api_base to litellm_params when configured
- **Impact**: Enables custom Ollama hosts

### Bug #5 (MEDIUM): Schema Format in fuzzer.py:105
- **Status**: Already fixed in previous commit
- **Fix**: Changed list value to string description

## Verification ✅

All fixes have been comprehensively verified:

- ✅ **Manual code review** - All fixes inspected line-by-line
- ✅ **Python syntax validated** - All modified files syntax-checked
- ✅ **LLM verification** - GPT-4o-mini independently verified all 5 fixes (PASS)
- ✅ **Project-wide scan** - 0 similar issues found (5,655 files scanned)
- ✅ **Documentation** - Enhanced with searchable tags for future maintenance

See `CURSOR_BOT_BUGS_FINAL_REPORT.md` for complete verification details.

## Key Features

### Unified LLM Interface
- Single `LLMClient` class for all providers
- Consistent API across OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Ollama, etc.
- Drop-in replacement for existing provider-specific code

### Automatic Fallback
- Primary → Fallback chain with configurable retry
- Graceful degradation on provider failures
- Task-specific model selection

### Cost Tracking
- Per-request cost calculation
- Budget limits with overflow protection
- Cost reporting and analytics

### Response Caching
- SHA-256 keyed cache
- Configurable cache directory
- Automatic cache invalidation

## Implementation Details

### Files Modified
- `packages/llm_analysis/llm/client.py` - Unified LLM client (Bug #2 fixed)
- `packages/llm_analysis/llm/providers.py` - LiteLLM provider (Bug #4 fixed)
- `packages/llm_analysis/llm/config.py` - LLM configuration
- `packages/llm_analysis/agent.py` - Analysis agent (Bug #3 fixed)
- `packages/web/fuzzer.py` - Web fuzzer (Bugs #1 and #5 fixed)

### Testing
- All existing tests passing
- New integration tests added
- Provider-specific validation

## Breaking Changes

None - The refactoring maintains backward compatibility with the existing API.

## Migration Notes

For existing code using provider-specific clients:
```python
# Before
from packages.llm_analysis.openai_client import OpenAIClient
client = OpenAIClient(api_key=key)

# After
from packages.llm_analysis.llm.client import LLMClient
from packages.llm_analysis.llm.config import LLMConfig, ModelConfig

config = LLMConfig(
    primary_model=ModelConfig(provider="openai", model_name="gpt-4"),
)
client = LLMClient(config)
```

## Security Enhancements

- ✅ API key sanitization in all error logs (Bug #2 fix)
- ✅ Defense-in-depth logging protection
- ✅ Comprehensive documentation with searchable security tags

## Documentation

- Updated README with LiteLLM integration guide
- Added configuration examples
- Documented fallback behavior
- Added searchable security tags for future maintenance

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> Replaces per-provider LLM code with a LiteLLM-based provider (with fallback/retry), adds structured generation and API key log sanitization, and updates agents/web modules and docs/deps accordingly.
> 
> - **LLM Infrastructure**:
>   - **Unified Provider**: Replace Anthropic/OpenAI/Ollama implementations with `LiteLLMProvider` using LiteLLM + Instructor; factory now always returns LiteLLM.
>   - **Structured Output**: Implement `_dict_schema_to_pydantic` and `generate_structured()` via Instructor; returns `(dict, full_response)`.
>   - **Security**: Add `_sanitize_log_message()` and enable LiteLLM redaction to prevent API key leakage; sanitize all error logs.
>   - **Retries/Cost/Cache**: Standardize exponential backoff (`retry_delay`), maintain caching and cost tracking in `LLMClient`.
>   - **Config**: Add Gemini default support; prefer general reasoning Ollama models; simplify default factories.
> - **Agents & Tools**:
>   - Update `agent.py`, `crash_agent.py`, `autonomous/dialogue.py` to new API (remove `task_type`, pass config, use `LLMProvider` types).
>   - Fix tuple unpacking for `generate_structured()` and construct dataclasses from returned dicts in CodeQL analyzer/dataflow validator.
>   - Gate patch generation to exploitable findings only; improve stats retrieval and logging.
> - **Web Scanning**:
>   - Update `web/fuzzer.py` and `web/scanner.py` to use `LLMProvider` and structured outputs; initialize `LLMClient` with `LLMConfig` in CLI.
> - **Dependencies & Docs**:
>   - `requirements.txt`: add `litellm`, `instructor`, `pydantic`; remove provider-specific SDKs.
>   - `README.md`: reorganize documentation sections and add AI assistant guides overview.
>

author: cyanoxygen
body: Some partitioning tools like ones based on libparted (parted and GParted) don't wipe the entire GPT partition name field before writing new partition names. Additionally, it is not guaranteed to be properly zeroed since the UEFI specification does not clearly state that. Current checksuming logic uses processed partition names which ignores garbage data after the null terminator, and reports an CRC error if such partition table is encountered: (This test program uses `gptman` to scan for ESP partition(s).) You can easily recreate this issue using either parted or GParted, first name a partition with a longer name, then rename it with a shorter name. You can see the remining bytes are not zeroed: Use a dedicated raw buffer which directly read or write to the disk to perform checksums without explicit string handling.

body:
Creates AvaloniaGRBL, a cross-platform UI foundation for LaserGRBL using Avalonia 11.3.9 on .NET 9.0.

## Implementation

- **Project structure**: MVVM architecture with ViewModels and Views following Avalonia conventions
- **Main window layout**: 
  - Menu bar with complete menu hierarchy (Grbl, File, Generate, Schema, Preview, Language, Tools, Help)
  - Split-panel view: left panel for connection and jog controls, right panel for G-code preview
  - Status bar with placeholders for lines, buffer, progress, time estimate, and status
- **Left panel controls**:
  - Connection section: COM port selector, baud rate dropdown, connect button
  - Jog controls: 8-way directional grid + home button, speed/step configuration
- **Right panel**: Toolbar buttons (Open, Start, Pause, Stop, Reset) and preview canvas area

All UI elements are non-functional placeholders. The application compiles and runs on Windows, Linux, and macOS.

## Build

```bash
cd AvaloniaGRBL/AvaloniaGRBL
dotnet build
dotnet run
```

## Screenshot

![AvaloniaGRBL UI](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e2e73f49-cbf4-4b42-8c1d-635d540cb3b3)

- Used Border instead of Separator in toolbar for cross-platform rendering consistency
- Removed template boilerplate from MainWindowViewModel

body:
Phase 3 scoring was referencing a non-existent module (`farfan_pipeline.analysis.scoring`), causing import failures. The interface contract between Phase 2 (EvidenceNexus) and Phase 3 (Scoring) was undefined, preventing score computation from evidence graphs.

## Implementation

- **Scoring engine** (`farfan_pipeline/analysis/scoring/scoring.py`, 783 lines)
  - 6 modality types (TYPE_A-F) with distinct thresholds and weight profiles
  - Evidence structure validator enforcing Phase 2 output contract
  - Quality level determination (EXCELLENT/GOOD/ADEQUATE/POOR)
  - Wilson score confidence intervals (Wilson 1927, JASA)

- **Mathematical foundation module** (`mathematical_foundation.py`, 530 lines) **[NEW]**
  - Three formal theorems with proofs and implementations
  - Wilson score interval (Wilson 1927, JASA) - proper confidence interval computation
  - Weighted convex combination theorem - guarantees score boundedness
  - Dempster-Shafer belief combination (Sentz & Ferson 2002) - evidence aggregation
  - Automated theorem verification functions

- **Interface validator** (`nexus_scoring_validator.py`, 418 lines)
  - 3-layer validation: schema, semantic, provenance (SHA-256)
  - Batch validation for 300-question corpus
  - Cross-phase contract enforcement at entry point

- **Test suite** (67 tests total, 100% passing)
  - `test_nexus_scoring_alignment.py` (35 tests) - interface contracts, modalities, adaptive thresholds
  - `test_mathematical_foundation.py` (32 tests) **[NEW]** - theorem verification, Wilson interval properties, convexity, Dempster-Shafer commutativity
  - 300-question integration test confirming stability

## Mathematical Foundation (v2.0 Enhancement)

### Academic References (All Real, Peer-Reviewed)

1. **Wilson, E. B. (1927)** "Probable inference, the law of succession, and statistical inference." *Journal of the American Statistical Association*, 22(158), 209-212. DOI: 10.1080/01621459.1927.10502953

2. **O'Neill, B. (2021)** "Mathematical properties and finite-population correction for the Wilson score interval." arXiv:2109.12464 [math.ST]

3. **Sentz, K., & Ferson, S. (2002)** "Combination of Evidence in Dempster-Shafer Theory." Sandia National Laboratories, SAND 2002-0835

4. **Han, D., Dezert, J., & Yang, Y. (2012)** "Evaluations of Evidence Combination Rules in Terms of Statistical Sensitivity and Divergence." *International Journal of Uncertainty, Fuzziness and Knowledge-Based Systems*

5. **Zhou, K., Martin, A., & Pan, Q. (2015)** "A belief combination rule for a large number of sources." *Journal of Advances in Information Fusion*, 10(1)

### Three Formal Theorems

**Theorem 1** (Wilson 1927): Wilson score confidence interval provides asymptotically correct coverage with better small-sample properties than Wald intervals.

**Theorem 2** (Convex Analysis): For scores s₁, ..., sₙ ∈ [0,1] and weights Σwᵢ = 1, the weighted mean satisfies min(sᵢ) ≤ Σwᵢsᵢ ≤ max(sᵢ) (convexity property).

**Theorem 3** (Sentz & Ferson 2002): Dempster's combination rule is commutative: m₁ ⊕ m₂ = m₂ ⊕ m₁.

## Interface Contract

```python
# Phase 2 output (EvidenceNexus)
evidence: dict = {
    "elements": list[dict],     # Evidence nodes
    "confidence": float,        # [0, 1]
    "graph_hash": str,          # SHA-256 provenance
}

# Phase 3 input (Scoring)
result = apply_scoring(evidence, modality="TYPE_A")
# => ScoredResult(score=0.87, quality_level=EXCELLENT, ...)
```

## Modality Specifications

| Type | Threshold | Weight (E/S/P) | Use Case |
|------|-----------|----------------|----------|
| TYPE_A | 0.75 | 0.5/0.3/0.2 | Quantitative indicators |
| TYPE_B | 0.65 | 0.3/0.3/0.4 | Qualitative patterns |
| TYPE_C | 0.60 | 0.33/0.34/0.33 | Mixed evidence |
| TYPE_D | 0.70 | 0.4/0.3/0.3 | Temporal series |
| TYPE_E | 0.65 | 0.35/0.35/0.3 | Territorial coverage |
| TYPE_F | 0.60 | 0.35/0.3/0.35 | Institutional actors |

*E=Elements, S=Similarity, P=Patterns*

## Validation

Entry point stabilization confirmed:
- **67/67 tests passing (100%)** - 35 interface + 32 mathematical theorem tests
- 300/300 questions validated with mathematical stability verified
- SISAS adaptive threshold integration verified
- Provenance tracking enforced (64-char SHA-256)
- Automated theorem verification (convexity, monotonicity, commutativity)

## Mathematical Guarantees

- **[INV-SC-001]** Score Boundedness: Guaranteed by Theorem 2 (convexity property)
- **[INV-SC-002]** Quality Determinism: Unique quality level for each score
- **[INV-SC-003]** Metadata Completeness: Contract enforcement validated
- **[INV-SC-004]** Confidence Calibration: Proper coverage by Theorem 1 (Wilson interval)

Comprehensive documentation: 
- `docs/NEXUS_SCORING_ALIGNMENT.md` - Interface specification
- `docs/MATHEMATICAL_FOUNDATION_SCORING.md` - Academic foundations with theorem proofs
- `SCORING_ENHANCEMENT_SUMMARY.md` - v1.0 → v2.0 enhancement overview

author: rjwalters
body:
## Summary

- The existing filter benchmark was testing the columnar SIMD execution path (~900µs) rather than the morsel-driven row filter (~5-30ms)
- Add `bench_morsel_filter_direct()` to test `morsel_parallel_filter` API directly, bypassing SQL/columnar execution
- Update documentation to clarify the difference between SQL-based and direct API benchmarks

## Root Cause Analysis

The original issue reported "Filter operations in the morsel benchmark show no parallel speedup."

Investigation revealed:
1. SQL queries (`SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ... WHERE ...`) route through the **columnar SIMD execution engine** by default
2. Columnar SIMD filter is ~100x faster than row-oriented execution (~900µs vs ~30ms for 500K rows)
3. The `morsel_parallel_filter` function was **never being called** because the queries used the columnar path
4. The benchmark was measuring columnar SIMD performance, not morsel parallelism

## Direct API Benchmark Results

The new direct API benchmark confirms **parallel speedup IS working** for `morsel_parallel_filter`:

| Predicate | 1T | 8T | Speedup |
|-----------|-----|-----|---------|
| 50% selectivity | 27.9ms | 15.2ms | **1.84x** |
| 10% selectivity | 4.5ms | 1.9ms | **2.37x** |
| 1% selectivity | 4.3ms | 1.2ms | **3.58x** |
| 25% compound | 14.0ms | 7.4ms | **1.90x** |

Lower selectivity predicates scale better because less output copying is needed. The 50% selectivity case is more memory-bound due to copying 250K result rows.

## Changes

- Add `bench_morsel_filter_direct()` function that tests `morsel_parallel_filter` using direct Rust API
- Add `OPERATION_FILTER=morsel_filter` option to run the direct API benchmark
- Update module documentation to clarify:
  - Direct API benchmarks (row-oriented, tests morsel work-stealing)
  - SQL-based benchmarks (columnar by default, SIMD-optimized)
- Reorder benchmarks to run direct API test first when running all benchmarks

## Test plan

- [x] Build benchmark with new code
- [x] Run `OPERATION_FILTER=morsel_filter` to verify direct API benchmark works
- [x] Verify parallel speedup is visible in direct API benchmark results
- [x] Run existing `OPERATION_FILTER=filter` to verify SQL benchmark still works

## Fixes for Code Review Issues

- [x] Fix extra closing brace at line 365 in MUApplicationDelegate.m
- [x] Remove reference to undefined _connectionActive variable (line 396)
- [x] Remove duplicate observer registrations (lines 302-303 vs 412-420)
- [x] Update MUAudioTransmissionPreferencesViewController.swift to call MUAudioSessionManager on transmission method changes
- [x] Fix AVAudioSessionCategoryOptions inconsistency (MixWithOthers vs DuckOthers)
- [x] Document redundant AVAudioSession configuration calls

## Changes Made

**MUApplicationDelegate.m:**
- Removed extra closing brace that was prematurely closing the @implementation block
- Fixed `applicationWillResignActive` and `applicationDidBecomeActive` to use `[MUConnectionController isConnected]` instead of undefined `_connectionActive`
- Removed duplicate AVAudioSession notification observer registrations from `registerForAppLifecycleNotifications` (kept them in `registerForAudioSessionNotifications`)
- Changed AVAudioSessionCategoryOptions from `DuckOthers` to `MixWithOthers` to match MUAudioCaptureManager configuration
- Fixed brace structure in `applicationDidBecomeActive`

**MUAudioTransmissionPreferencesViewController.swift:**
- Added call to `MUAudioSessionManager.shared.updateTransmitMethod(withString:)` when transmission method changes to keep audio configuration in sync

## Notes on Redundant AVAudioSession Configuration

The setupAudio method currently has multiple AVAudioSession configuration paths:
1. `configureAudioSessionWithDefaults` (line 175)
2. `MUAudioSessionManager.shared.configureSession` (line 176)
3. `MUAudioCaptureManager refreshEncoderPreferences` (called from line 255)
4. Final activation check (lines 263-265)

This is intentional as each component manages different aspects:
- `configureAudioSessionWithDefaults`: Sets category, mode, and options based on preprocessor and transmission settings
- `MUAudioSessionManager`: Manages VAD thresholds and codec quality presets
- `MUAudioCaptureManager`: Configures sample rate and buffer duration for the capture pipeline

While redundant, consolidating these would require refactoring the architecture of how these three managers interact, which is beyond the scope of resolving merge conflicts.

This implements `cargo report timings` HTML replay feature.

The help text looks like:

```
Reports the build timings of previous builds (unstable)

Usage: cargo report timings [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --open              Opens the timing report in a browser
      ...
```


Part of <https://github.com/rust-lang/cargo/issues/15844>

### How to test and review this PR?

Open questions:

* [ ] The replayed HTML report will be written to
  * If in a Cargo workspace, write to `<artifact-dir>/cargo-timings/`
  * Otherwise, write to a temp directory
* [ ] The log discovery logic 
  * Currently look at the newest log file for the workspace.
  * If not in a workspace, pick the newest log file in the log directory.
* [ ] Snapshots HTML report and log files are added.

author: simonosipov
body:
## Summary

Fixes the Lighthouse CI status check in `.github/workflows/preview.yml` that was incorrectly using GitHub's `pending` state as a "warning" state for Lighthouse scores below target but above failure thresholds.

### Problem
- GitHub interprets `pending` as "waiting for result," causing PR checks to appear stuck/incomplete
- This caused confusion in PR status and could block merging with branch protection rules

### Solution
Changed the status logic to:
- Use `success` state for all passing/warning scores (state is either `success` or `failure`, never `pending`)
- Add descriptive emojis in the status description to indicate severity:
  | Score Range | Status | Description |
  |-------------|--------|-------------|
  | Desktop 80+, Mobile 70+ | `success` | `Desktop: X, Mobile: Y` |
  | Desktop 60-79, Mobile 50-69 | `success` | `⚠️ Desktop: X, Mobile: Y (below target)` |
  | Desktop <60 or Mobile <50 | `failure` | `❌ Desktop: X, Mobile: Y (below minimum)` |

### Files Changed
- `.github/workflows/preview.yml` - Updated "Set Lighthouse Status Check" step (lines 546-568)

## Test Plan
- [ ] PR is created and CI runs successfully
- [ ] Lighthouse status check shows as `success` (green check) or `failure` (red X), never `pending` (yellow dot)
- [ ] Warning-level scores display with ⚠️ emoji in the status description
- [ ] Failure-level scores display with ❌ emoji in the status description
- [ ] PR comment in report-results job still shows correct yellow/green/red icons for Lighthouse

author: cai360
body:
This change removes all `ondelete="CASCADE"`  into `ondelete="set null` from foreign keys referencing users.id.

Our domain requires soft deletion for users—meaning a user account may be deactivated, but its historical records must remain intact. From my opinion, company should keep the record of the assignment history.

Reason: 
1. Users are soft-deleted, not physically removed
The system never hard-deletes a user. Instead, deleted_at is set.
With soft delete:
	•	The user still exists in the DB
	•	Their historical actions must remain traceable
	•	FK cascading is not appropriate, because nothing should be removed when a user is soft-deleted
2. Companies must retain historical records

3. Keeping SET NULL also preserves future flexibility
Even though we use soft delete today, adding SET NULL ensures the schema is safe in the future in case:
	•	we introduce hard deletion for certain user scenarios


---
Company deletion is different, company deletion is allowed to cascade because:
	•	When a company is deleted, all its shifts, leave requests, assignments, etc. become meaningless.
	•	This is a valid case for ON DELETE CASCADE.

## Summary

Implements Phase 1 + 1b of the alignment tool for onboarding existing translation repositories.

### What's New

**Phase 1: Structural Diagnostics**
- **`tool-alignment/`** - New CLI tool for alignment diagnostics
- **Structural Analyzer** - Compares sections, subsections, code blocks, math blocks, heading-maps
- **Config File Analysis** - Supports `_toc.yml`, `_config.yml`, `environment.yml`
- **Report Generator** - Markdown + JSON output with scoring methodology

**Phase 1b: Code Block Integrity Check**
- **Code Extraction** - `{code-cell}` directives + standard markdown blocks
- **Normalized Comparison** - Filters out translation differences:
  - Strings → `"<< STRING >>"`
  - Comments → `# << COMMENT >>`
  - Captions → `caption: << CAPTION >>`
- **LCS Diff Algorithm** - Accurate line-by-line diff showing only code logic changes
- **5-Tier Scoring** - ✅ 100%, 🟨 90-99%, 🟡 80-89%, 🟠 60-79%, 🔴 <60%
- **Localization Detection** - Flags CJK font config patterns with 📍 i18n note
- **Dual Reports** - `*-structure.md` and `*-code.md`

### Test Coverage

- **88 tests passing** (51 new for Phase 1b)
- 14 test fixtures covering all alignment and code integrity scenarios

### Real-World Validation

Tested against `lecture-python-intro` → `lecture-intro.zh-cn`:

**Structure Alignment:**
| Status | Count | % |
|--------|-------|---|
| ✅ Aligned | 38 | 69% |
| 🟡 Likely aligned | 8 | 15% |
| ⚠️ Needs review | 2 | 4% |
| ❌ Diverged | 3 | 5% |
| 📄 Missing | 2 | 4% |
| ➕ Extra | 2 | 4% |

**Code Block Integrity:**
| Metric | Value |
|--------|-------|
| Overall Score | **79%** (717/906 blocks) |
| Matched | 717 |
| Modified | 186 |
| Missing | 3 |
| Extra | 4 |

### Usage

```bash
cd tool-alignment
npm install

# Generate all reports
npm run diagnose -- -s <source> -t <target> -o reports/output -r all

# Structure report only
npm run diagnose -- -s <source> -t <target> -o reports/output -r structure

# Code report only  
npm run diagnose -- -s <source> -t <target> -o reports/output -r code
```

### Next Steps

- Phase 2: Haiku Quality Scoring (per-section assessment)
- Phase 3: Heading-Map Generator
- Phase 4: Interactive Alignment PR
- Phase 5: GitHub Action Integration

body:
Addresses CVE-2025-55182, a critical remote code execution vulnerability in React Server Components. Current version 10.1.3 is vulnerable; Vercel has blocked deployments of unpatched versions.

## Changes

- **Next.js**: 10.1.3 → 15.5.7 (patched version)
- **React/React-DOM**: 17.0.2 → 18.2.0 (required peer dependency for Next.js 15)
- **Removed** `next-images` (functionality now built-in)
- **Fixed** `react-lite-toast` SSR failure caused by SVG imports in CommonJS build:

```javascript
// Before: import { Toast } from "react-lite-toast"
const Toast = dynamic(() => import("react-lite-toast").then((mod) => mod.Toast), {
  ssr: false,
});
```

- Uses `--legacy-peer-deps` due to unmaintained dependencies (`react-bootstrap@0.33.1`, `react-isotope@1.0.7`)
- These packages continue to function correctly with React 18
- Static site generation verified working (6/6 pages)

I hereby agree to the terms of the [GreptimeDB CLA](https://github.com/GreptimeTeam/.github/blob/main/CLA.md).

## Refer to a related PR or issue link (optional)
#6558 
## What's changed and what's your intention?

This PR implements the `copy_region_from` API for the mito2 engine, which is a critical step in the repartition procedure when adding new metric regions.

**Background:**
During the repartition procedure, when a new region is created, it needs to copy parquet files from existing regions to obtain the metadata required for creating logical tables. This operation ensures that the new region has the necessary data files to properly serve the logical tables.

**Changes:**
- Add `copy_region_from` API to `RegionEngine` trait for copying SST files from a source region to a target region within the same table
- Implement the `copy_region_from` functionality in mito2 engine with parallel file copying and automatic cleanup on failure
- Add `RegionFileCopier` utility for file copying operations with proper source/target path handling for both data and index files
- Move `RegionMetadataLoader` to a new `region/utils.rs` module for better organization
- Add mock layer support for copy operation interceptor in object-store for testing

author: galarzafrancisco
body:
## Summary

This PR implements the **Token Exchange Feature** (RFC 8693 compliant) that enables MCP Servers to exchange their MCP access tokens for downstream system tokens (e.g., Google Cloud, GitHub) without requiring end-users to re-authenticate.

### Key Features

- **Seamless Token Exchange**: MCP servers present their JWT and request downstream tokens
- **Scope Mapping**: Automatically resolves MCP scopes to downstream provider scopes
- **Security Controls**: 
  - Prevents scope escalation (can only request subset of entitled scopes)
  - Validates MCP JWT signatures using existing JWKS infrastructure
  - Automatic token refresh with 5-minute expiration buffer
- **Flexible Connection Identification**: Supports lookup by both UUID and human-readable providedId

### Backend Implementation

#### Database Changes
- Added \`providedId\` column to \`mcp_connections\` table (unique, nullable, varchar 255)
- Migration file created for schema update

#### New Services & DTOs
- \`TokenExchangeService\`: Core token exchange logic with JWT validation, scope resolution, and automatic refresh
- \`TokenExchangeRequestDto\`: RFC 8693 compliant request validation
- \`TokenExchangeResponseDto\`: RFC 8693 compliant response structure

#### API Endpoint
\`\`\`
POST /auth/token-exchange/mcp/:serverIdentifier/:version
\`\`\`

Request body:
\`\`\`json
{
  "grant_type": "urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange",
  "subject_token": "MCP_JWT_TOKEN",
  "subject_token_type": "urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:access_token",
